title: Unique functorial decalage of a filtered cochain complex
statement: Let C be abelian, K an integer cochain complex, and F a decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration]. There is a unique decreasing filtration D with degree n step D^a=F^(a+n) intersect the inverse image of F^(a+n+1) under d. Every map of filtered cochain complexes preserves these decalage filtrations with the same underlying cochain map. No boundedness or finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

source.document: Stacks Project, Homological Algebra and Derived Categories

proof.text: Take the intersection of each filtration step with the indicated differential inverse image. Square zero ensures that the differential lands in the next intersection, so restriction through the monic inclusions defines a subcomplex. Monotonicity of the filtration and pullback gives its decreasing transitions. Its image in every degree is the prescribed subobject.

Reuse the proved filtered_step_preserved, subobject_preserves_pullback and subobject_preserves_inf helpers from FilteredQuotientPageMaps. Their hypotheses are for arbitrary filtered cochain maps, with no finiteness requirement. These show that a filtered cochain map preserves the first intersected step and the inverse-image step by the differential commutation equation. Restrict it degreewise and cancel the monic inclusions to obtain the cochain map on each step.
Equal prescribed degreewise subobjects give subcomplex inclusions in both directions. Antisymmetry proves equality of every step, and function extensionality proves uniqueness of the filtration.

Choose the uniquely characterized filtration and give its degreewise formula. The proved preservation property restricts each underlying filtered map; these restrictions define the decalage endofunctor. Identity and composition hold definitionally on the underlying maps and by proof irrelevance on their preservation witnesses.

lean.statement:
theorem exists_decalage {C : Type u} [Category.{v} C] [Abelian C]
    {K : CochainComplex C ℤ} (F : DecreasingFiltration K) :
    ∃! D : DecreasingFiltration K, (∀ a n : ℤ,
      D.complexStep a n = F.complexStep (a + n) n ⊓
        (Subobject.pullback (K.d n (n + 1))).obj
          (F.complexStep (a + n + 1) (n + 1))) ∧
      ∀ {K' : CochainComplex C ℤ} (F' D' : DecreasingFiltration K'),
        (∀ a n : ℤ, D'.complexStep a n = F'.complexStep (a + n) n ⊓
          (Subobject.pullback (K'.d n (n + 1))).obj
            (F'.complexStep (a + n + 1) (n + 1))) →
        ∀ t : (⟨K, F⟩ : FilteredObject (CochainComplex C ℤ)) ⟶ ⟨K', F'⟩,
          ∃ s : (⟨K, D⟩ : FilteredObject (CochainComplex C ℤ)) ⟶ ⟨K', D'⟩,
            s.hom = t.hom
